{{Short description|American physicist (1930–2012)}}
{{Orphan|date=October 2017}}

'''Julian Clifford Holmes''' (November 20, 1930 – December 16, 2012) was an American physicist, rocket scientist, inventor, political activist and environmental [[Social gadfly|gadfly.]]

Holmes was born in Portland, Maine.  The son of mathematics teachers Cecil T. and Marion C. Holmes, he studied physics at [[Bowdoin College]], from which he was hired in 1951, by the Rocketry Division of the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory]] (NRL) in Washington, D.C, where he spent his entire career, retiring as a GS 14 Government physicist on December 30, 1985.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://siarchives.si.edu/research/videohistory_catalog9539.html|title=Smithsonian Institution Archives|publisher=}}</ref>

At NRL, Holmes’ career evolved with the [[Cold War]]. He developed countermeasure sensors for detecting distant nuclear events, and designed aeronomy instrumentation for the Navy's [[Aerobee]] class of scientific rockets during the Navy's technological transition from [[cathode ray tube]] electronics to [[solid-state electronics]]. He also developed formulas for interpreting data captured by these rockets' returning payloads, bringing a better understanding of the nature of the earth's [[ionosphere]], and of the effects of solar fluxes and manmade chemicals on it.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://collections.si.edu/search/results.htm?view=&dsort=&date.slider=&q=Aerobee%20rockets,%20holmes|title=Search results for: Aerobee rockets, holmes, page 1 - Collections Search Center, Smithsonian Institution|publisher=}}</ref>

In the course of his work, Holmes was awarded six patents for inventions relating to [[electronic countermeasures]], development of instrumentation for the [[Aerobee]] rocket series, and for interpretation of data from Aerobee and other rockets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO2&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=/netahtml/PTO/search-bool.html&r=11&f=G&l=50&co1=AND&d=PALL&s1=4,006,404&OS=4,006,404&RS=4,006,404|title=United States Patent: 5033404 - Barrier mechanism for isolating drive chain from active chamber in Langmuir trough|publisher=}}</ref>

In addition to his scientific and engineering achievements, Holmes was a citizen activist,  stimulating reforms in rural [[Maryland]] county zoning laws in the 1960s and 1970s.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Sewage Is Gadfly's Concern | url=http://penbay.org/searsisland/julian_holmes/holmesgadfly_1970.jpg | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131101151207/http://penbay.org/searsisland/julian_holmes/holmesgadfly_1970.jpg | archive-date=2013-11-01}}</ref>  Holmes  used [[Grand juries]] to investigate corruption in the 1980s.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Grand Jury Hears Holmes; Rt. 5 Opening Still Vague | url=http://penbay.org/searsisland/julian_holmes/holmes_grandjury_pg_sentinel_091689.jpg | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131101151247/http://penbay.org/searsisland/julian_holmes/holmes_grandjury_pg_sentinel_091689.jpg | archive-date=2013-11-01}}</ref>  In 1993 Holmes returned to [[Maine]] with companion Audrey Marra.  There he helped enact a ban on the sale of controversial gasoline additive [[MTBE]] in that state.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Dirty air, dirty water the politics of cartest and oxygenated gasoline - How Corporate Power Compromises Public Health Environmental Quality and Government Integrity | url=http://snakeroot.net/Julian/DADW120.TXT | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060517012117/http://www.snakeroot.net:80/Julian/DADW120.TXT | archive-date=2006-05-17}}</ref> He became an advocate for forestry reform and island conservation, playing a key role in the rejection of an industrial port on pristine [[Sears Island]] in [[Penobscot Bay]].<ref>{{Cite web| title=Letter to Julian C. Holmes | url=http://penbay.org/searsisland/julian_holmes/holmes_si_mdot_020596.jpg | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131101150723/http://penbay.org/searsisland/julian_holmes/holmes_si_mdot_020596.jpg | archive-date=2013-11-01}}</ref>

Holmes died in [[Lewiston, Maine]] on December 16, 2012.
